key_insight: First-principles calculations predict ferroelectric ground states in 11 of 15 [111]-oriented perovskite-oxide superlattices, with octahedral rotations sometimes substantially changing ferroelectric properties.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for octahedral rotations can guide the design of ferroelectric oxide heterostructures, although the abstract reports no AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Calculate ground-state structures of 15 free-standing superlattices from first principles.
Analyze zone-center phonons and force constants to interpret structural distortions and ferroelectricity.
Compare thermodynamic stability for [111] and [100] growth orientations.
evidence_signal: The computational survey identifies 11 ferroelectric ground states among 15 superlattices and finds that both polar distortions and octahedral rotations are described by Γ-point phonons.
watch_item: Predictions for free-standing structures require validation under practical substrate strain and growth conditions.
paper_title: Properties of [111]-oriented ferroelectric superlattices based on oxides with a perovskite structure
